causal_graphs.context: Incubate 100 uM HxlR with 1 mM formaldehyde in 20 mM HEPES pH 7.5 and 300 mM NaCl for 1 h at 37 C; desalt by Micro Bio-Spin 6 and analyze by Bruker Solarix XR FT-MS. Purification removes the N-terminal His tag with thrombin, followed by DTT treatment and SEC. The structural preparation retains a GSH cleavage extension.

evidence.explanation: Supplementary Figure 1c was visually inspected with FT-MS Methods; Figure 1a/c/d and Supplementary Note 3 provide separate chemical-assignment evidence and its limits.
Exact reference/PDB sequence checks establish intact-protein scope and show that C11/K13 are outside the current Pfam boundary.

edges.mechanism: Formaldehyde treatment produces new intact-protein mass peaks displaced by 12 Da relative to untreated HxlR. Cross-assay evidence supports a C11/K13 methylene bridge, but the directly observed edge is the chemical-product mass response, not every proposed bond-forming microstep.
edges.subject: formaldehyde-purified-hxlr

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P42406 sequence version 3 is 120 aa; UniProt/InterPro sequences match, with PF01638 at 19-107. PDB 7BZD entity 1 is exactly GSH plus this reference. C11 and K13 are outside the current Pfam interval. The experiment therefore concerns an intact domain-bearing protein, not chemistry by the isolated Pfam domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: Intact-mass spectra establish new plus-12-Da species, not their unique chemical topology alone. Separate crystal density, cellular tryptic MS/MS and synthetic-peptide substitutions support the C11/K13 methylene assignment. Those samples are not one time-resolved reaction trajectory. Unmodified and sodium-adduct species persist; no quantitative yield, chemical reversibility or obligatory sequential intermediate is asserted.

nodes.label: Treat purified intact HxlR with 1 mM formaldehyde
HxlR species with a plus-12-Da intact mass shift

causal_graphs.scope: Purified B. subtilis 168 HxlR expressed from pET28a in E. coli BL21(DE3), Zhu 2021 Supplementary Figure 1c; not the synthetic peptide, cellular MS/MS or FAsor fusion assay.
causal_graphs.title: Formaldehyde produces a plus-12-Da species of purified intact HxlR

causal_graphs.context: EMSA Methods pretreat 100 uM protein with or without 1 mM formaldehyde for 1-2 h at 37 C in 20 mM HEPES pH 7.5 and 300 mM NaCl. Figure 1e instead labels 0.6 mM formaldehyde; this discrepancy remains unresolved. Final WT/C11A protein is 0.2, 0.4 or 0.6 uM in 20 ul with 50 nM 50-bp BRH duplex, 20 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 50 mM KCl, 5 mM MgCl2 and 10% glycerol. Table 2 specifies BRH-F/R, not the optimized 20-bp crystallization duplex. Representative gels from three independent experiments.

evidence.explanation: Figure 1e was visually inspected with EMSA Methods and Table 2. Protein concentration, DNA identity and conflicting formaldehyde labels are explicit.

edges.mechanism: At matched WT protein concentrations, formaldehyde-treated samples shift more BRH DNA than untreated samples. This records the direct binding response without assigning an observed allosteric trajectory or native operon output.
edges.subject: formaldehyde-wt-binding

evidence.explanation: The WT/C11A paired treatment lanes in Figure 1e and Results establish the response difference, with nonzero C11A binding retained.

edges.mechanism: C11A shows little additional shift after formaldehyde treatment compared with WT's positive response over the matched 0.2-0.6-uM series. Its residual basal binding prevents calling the protein binding-null, and the mutation does not isolate the contribution of the Pfam domain.
edges.subject: c11a-binding

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P42406 / B. subtilis 168 reference 1-120 contains PF01638 19-107; C11 is outside that interval. The N-terminal His tag is thrombin-cleaved, with GSH retained in the sequence-verified structural preparation. Neither C11A nor WT is an isolated Pfam-domain construct.
causal_graphs.limitations: Gel-shift enhancement is a direct biochemical binding response, not a measured transcription rate or fitted KD. C11A retains basal binding; lack of enhancement is not complete loss of DNA binding. Equal mutant folding and active fraction are not established by these gels. The formaldehyde concentration discrepancy is not resolved by assumed dilution, and static structural differences do not directly observe helix flipping.

nodes.label: BRH DNA in the shifted HxlR-DNA complex
Formaldehyde-dependent enhancement of the DNA gel shift

causal_graphs.scope: Purified pET28a-derived WT and C11A HxlR, Zhu 2021 Figure 1e; separate from cellular reporter and K13A titrations.
causal_graphs.title: Formaldehyde enhances WT HxlR DNA binding, with little enhancement in C11A

causal_graphs.context: Supplementary Figure 2d uses 0.05, 0.1, 0.15 and 0.2 uM K13A, with or without treatment labeled 0.6 mM formaldehyde. Shared EMSA Methods specify 1 mM pretreatment of 100 uM protein for 1-2 h at 37 C, followed by dilution into 50 nM BRH duplex with HEPES pH 7.0, KCl, MgCl2 and glycerol. The formaldehyde discrepancy is unresolved. Representative gel from three independent experiments; the WT positive response is from the separate Figure 1e range.

evidence.explanation: Supplementary Figure 2d and its caption were visually inspected, with the lower protein range and retained basal binding explicitly separated from Figure 1e.
evidence.snippet: the K13A mutant (HxlR-K13A) also remained insensitive to FA

edges.mechanism: Unlike the WT positive response, K13A shows little treatment-dependent enhancement across its tested 0.05-0.2-uM range while retaining DNA binding. The net loss of responsiveness is observed; loss of all binding or equal-concentration affinity comparisons are not asserted.
edges.subject: k13a-binding

causal_graphs.family_mapping: K13 is verified in P42406 and lies outside PF01638 19-107. The intact pET28a-derived HxlR mutant is tested, not the isolated HxlR-like domain. The 7BZD sequence check concerns WT structural protein, not an independently resequenced K13A assay stock.
causal_graphs.limitations: The edge denotes loss of the WT treatment response, not lower absolute DNA binding at identical WT/K13A concentrations. K13A retains strong basal shifts and the authors describe higher basal binding. Different concentration ranges do not establish a quantitative affinity ratio. Directness is confined to the biochemical response; a unique structural intermediate or conformational trajectory is not demonstrated.

nodes.label: K13A HxlR in its separate low-concentration titration
WT-like formaldehyde-dependent enhancement of BRH DNA binding

causal_graphs.scope: Purified K13A HxlR in Zhu 2021 Supplementary Figure 2d; its titration range differs from WT/C11A Figure 1e.
causal_graphs.title: K13A HxlR binds DNA but lacks the WT formaldehyde enhancement

causal_graphs.context: Dilute overnight cultures 1:100 into LB, grow to OD600 0.6, induce HxlR with 4 mM L-arabinose for 1 h, then treat with or without 600 uM formaldehyde for 40 min. Measure GFP by flow cytometry at 488-nm excitation and 530/30BP emission. Supplementary Figure 2b/c provides colony-count viability controls and scatter gating. These are not the purified pET28a constructs or native B. subtilis cultures.

evidence.explanation: Figure 1f and Supplementary Figure 2e WT controls, flow-cytometry Methods and the separate viability/gating panels establish the scoped fluorescence increase.

edges.mechanism: Formaldehyde shifts the WT-labeled reporter strain's GFP distribution toward greater fluorescence. The measured cellular endpoint is consistent with HxlR-dependent promoter activation but does not directly measure RNA synthesis or formaldehyde clearance.
edges.subject: formaldehyde-wt-reporter

evidence.explanation: Figure 1f paired WT/C11A treatment distributions and Methods support decreased reporter responsiveness, not isolated-domain chemistry.

edges.mechanism: The C11A reporter strain shows little formaldehyde-dependent GFP induction relative to the WT-labeled strain. Its lower basal signal is retained as a distinct observation, not evidence that only a single chemical step changed.
edges.subject: c11a-reporter

evidence.explanation: Supplementary Figure 2e was visually inspected with its caption and Results; both high basal signal and the weak treatment response are retained.
evidence.snippet: the K13A mutant (HxlR-K13A) also remained insensitive to FA

edges.mechanism: K13A has high basal GFP signal but little additional formaldehyde-dependent induction compared with the WT-labeled strain. This is a loss of responsiveness, not a globally inactive transcriptional regulator or a GFP-null phenotype.
edges.subject: k13a-reporter

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The source gene is P42406 from B. subtilis 168, with current PF01638 19-107; C11 and K13 are outside that interval. Supplementary Table 2's pBAD forward primer is compatible with an MGRM start instead of reference MSRM if translated from its apparent start, but Methods describe Gibson assembly. A primer-implied S2G possibility remains unresolved; author WT/C11A/K13A labels do not prove exact native N-terminal sequence.
causal_graphs.limitations: GFP distributions are indirect reporter phenotypes, not direct transcription-rate, formaldehyde-detoxification or native-operon measurements. C11A has lower basal reporter signal, whereas K13A has higher basal signal and little further induction. Viability/gating controls do not establish equal mutant protein abundance, folding or localization. The pBAD sequence discrepancy is preserved rather than claiming a resequenced WT plasmid. Separate biochemical and cellular assays are not joined into one observed trajectory.

nodes.label: Add 600 uM formaldehyde to the WT-labeled HxlR reporter strain

causal_graphs.scope: E. coli BW25113 carrying pBAD-HxlR constructs labeled WT, C11A or K13A and a B. subtilis 168 hxlAB-promoter GFP reporter, Zhu 2021 Figure 1f and Supplementary Figure 2e.
causal_graphs.title: HxlR substitutions reduce the formaldehyde-induced GFP reporter response in E. coli

record.description: HxlR, a member of this family, is a DNA-binding protein that acts as a positive regulator of the formaldehyde-inducible hxlAB operon in Bacillus subtilis.

evidence.explanation: Preserve the 1-versus-0.6-mM EMSA discrepancy, lower K13A protein range, primer-implied S2G possibility, GSH extension and C11/K13 positions outside the current Pfam interval. C11A peptide loses both plus-12 and plus-30 products, whereas K13A retains plus-30; neither peptide is an isolated Pfam domain.
The 2005 native-regulation study is cited by Zhu but was not independently retrieved and reviewed here; no native knockout/rescue edges are inferred from that citation.

discussions.notes: FAsor fusion engineering, methylglyoxal responses, HypR/YodB/QsrR and structural-motion interpretations require separate scope. Partial scientific self-review; IN_PROGRESS.
discussions.prompt: Resolve the pBAD N-terminal sequence and EMSA formaldehyde concentrations, then extend native-regulation and family-member coverage using separately verified experiments.
discussions.rationale: Seven observed assay effects do not directly establish the complete allosteric trajectory, native hxlAB regulation in B. subtilis, chemical reversibility or a shared ligand mechanism across PF01638.
